citeAs: Antol, S., Agrawal, A., Lu, J., Mitchell, M., Batra, D., Zitnick, C. L., and Parikh, D. (2015). VQA: Visual question answering. The IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV).
creator: S. Antol, A. Agrawal, J. Lu, M. Mitchell, D. Batra, C. L. Zitnick, D. Parikh
description: The VQA Dataset is a visual question answering dataset consisting of both real images from COCO and abstract cartoon images. The COCO-VQA portion has three questions per image with ten answers per question, and the synthetic SYNTH-VQA portion contains 50,000 cartoon scenes with three questions per scene and ten ground truth answers per question.
name: The VQA Dataset
rai:annotationsPerItem: 10 answers per question; COCO-VQA also has 3 questions per image.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The dataset uses 10 independent answers per question for a consensus-based evaluation metric. The paper reports inter-human agreement on COCO-VQA of about 83.3% and discusses disagreement, including subjective questions and cases where yes/no answers conflict.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For COCO-VQA, Amazon Mechanical Turk workers were asked to 'Stump a smart robot' to generate questions for each image, and a separate pool of workers generated the answers. Each question was answered by 10 independent annotators. The multiple-choice version includes the correct answer, plausible answers from annotators answering without seeing the image, popular answers from the dataset, and random answers from other questions.
rai:dataBiases: The paper states that many COCO-VQA questions can be accurately answered without using the image due to language biases. It also notes that the dataset contains many subjective and opinion-seeking questions, explanation-seeking questions, a heavy prevalence of yes/no questions (about 38% of all questions), and that almost 59% of yes/no questions are answered with 'yes'. For SYNTH-VQA, the paper says synthetic images can reduce natural-image context biases.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset combines real images from COCO and abstract synthetic cartoon scenes. COCO-VQA contains three human-generated questions per image and ten answers per question. SYNTH-VQA contains 50,000 synthetic scenes depicting cartoon images in simulated scenarios, with three questions per scene and ten ground truth answers per question.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Real images from the Microsoft COCO dataset and synthetic cartoon scenes. The synthetic scenes are made from over 100 different objects, 30 different animal models, and 20 human cartoon models.
rai:dataLimitations: The paper identifies multiple limitations: many questions can be answered from language alone; the dataset contains subjective, opinion-seeking, explanatory, and verbose questions that lack a single objective answer; inter-human agreement is only about 83%; and dataset biases plus the evaluation metric make it difficult to assess whether algorithms are truly solving VQA.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: A portion of the dataset uses synthetic cartoon imagery (SYNTH-VQA). The dataset is also provided in both open-ended and multiple-choice formats; the multiple-choice format adds 18 answer choices composed of the correct answer, plausible answers, popular answers, and random answers.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper describes VQA applications including aiding blind and visually impaired individuals by allowing them to query images on the web and in the real world, improving human-computer interaction, and supporting image retrieval.
rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluating visual question answering systems on both real-world and synthetic imagery.
